description: Routing eval for the resolved-incident write-up boundary: postmortem owns the retro on a finished incident, while near-miss vocabulary (sprint ceremonies, visual 'retro' styling, forensic postmortems, a still-live outage) must reach none of this cluster's members. self-improve-loop retired 2026-09-02 (unshipped, explicit-invocation only) along with the learning-lifecycle positives and self-improve-loop-narrowed negatives it anchored here, and prompt-engineer left the member list the same day when it folded into prompt-craft; root-cause, runbook, and prompt-craft remain as members purely for the whole-cluster negative default below, with no dedicated positive case of their own left in this file.
notes: Folded in from the retired retro-boundary.json cluster (self-improve-loop vs postmortem) on 2026-09-02: only its postmortem-side cases survive self-improve-loop's retirement, so they moved here rather than leaving a one-member file. The four ordinary negatives below rely on the whole-cluster default for expect_not_fires (four members now, not two), which is a strictly stronger assertion than their original two-member default and was checked case by case for safety before the move.

cases.prompt: Last night's NAS outage is resolved and everything is healthy again. Do a retro on the outage and write it up properly.
Facilitate a sprint retrospective for my team's Tuesday ceremony — agenda, icebreaker, and a template for action items.
Restyle this landing page with a retro 80s synthwave look — neon grid, chrome type, the works.
For a story I'm writing: what does a postmortem examination involve in forensic pathology, step by step?
Grafana is down right now — every dashboard is blank and the household is asking. Help.
